Months are divisions of the year used in calendars, serving as a way to organize time and track the passage of days. Each month varies in length, typically comprising either 28, 30, or 31 days, and they play a significant role in marking seasonal changes and important events.

In many cultures, months are named after historical figures, natural phenomena, or significant events, reflecting cultural traditions and historical significance. The concept of months is closely tied to the lunar and solar cycles, with some calendars being based on the phases of the moon while others align with the solar year.
